faq: Will custom code slow my site down?
We keep it light. Scripts load after the main content, unused code is left out and large libraries are avoided unless you need them. We check page speed before and after and tell you the difference.
Do I need a paid plan to use custom code?
Custom code areas are tied to your Webflow plan. We check your plan first and tell you what is possible before we start, so you never pay for work your plan cannot publish.
Can you fix code someone else wrote?
Yes, if it is JavaScript or CSS inside your Webflow project. We find the cause, fix it and note what changed. If the code is large or tangled, we may recommend rewriting that part.
Do you add tracking pixels here?

Simple tracking scripts, yes. For a full analytics and tag setup, our integrations and SEO services are a better fit. We follow each platform's rules and never add scripts that collect data without consent.
desc:
Webflow custom code and interactions add features the Designer cannot build on its own, such as custom filters, widgets, calculators and scroll animations. Ecom Swift LLC writes clean JavaScript and CSS and installs it safely in your project.

## What is Webflow custom code?

Webflow custom code is JavaScript, CSS or embed markup added to a project through its custom code areas or an embed element. The Designer covers a great deal, but some jobs need logic: filtering a list by several fields, switching currencies, validating a multi-step form or pulling data from another service.

Code is not a replacement for good design work. It fills the gaps. Done well, it sits quietly beside your visual build and never gets in the way of editing.

## Why clean code matters on a visual platform

The risk with custom code is not that it fails on day one. The risk is that it breaks six months later when someone renames a class, moves a section or adds a new page. Scripts pasted from forums often target fragile selectors, load too early or conflict with each other.

Careful code avoids those traps. It targets stable attributes, runs after the page has loaded, scopes itself to the pages that need it and explains itself in comments. A future developer, or you, can read it and understand what each part does.

## How custom features affect your visitors and your results

A good custom feature removes a task from the visitor. A calculator gives an instant answer, a live filter saves scrolling, and a booking widget saves a phone call. Each one shortens the route from interest to action.

Weight is the other side of the story. Every script costs loading time, especially on phones. That is why we load scripts after page content, keep them small, avoid duplicate libraries and host larger files on a CDN. The aim is a feature that helps without making the page heavier than it needs to be.

## What well-made Webflow custom code includes

- Plain JavaScript and CSS, with no unnecessary libraries.
- Code added to a single page when only one page needs it.
- Stable selectors, such as custom attributes, instead of fragile class chains.
- Clear comments that explain purpose and settings.
- Scripts that load after content, so first paint is not delayed.
- Mobile and browser testing before handover.
- Third-party widgets embedded and styled to match your design.
- Interactions that respect reduced-motion preferences.
- Fallbacks so a failed script does not break the page.
- Short usage notes, or a developer handover document for larger builds.

## How we build it

We begin by reading what you want the feature to do and checking whether Webflow can already do it natively. If the Designer can handle it, we say so and save you the cost. If not, we plan the smallest piece of code that does the job.

The Basic package installs one small script or embed, limited to the right page and tested on phone and desktop. The Standard package covers up to three custom scripts, one advanced interaction, a styled third-party widget and short usage notes. The Premium package handles a larger feature, such as a custom calculator or data pulled from an API, with code hosted on a CDN and a developer handover document. An extra script, a page speed check and a cookie consent banner are available as add-ons.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe the behavior you want from the visitor's point of view.
- Keep custom code in one place where you can find it.
- Test after every site change that touches the affected section.
- Ask for comments and a short note on how to adjust settings.
- Check a paid hosting or site plan if you plan to use custom code.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting snippets from unknown sources into the project.
- Loading the same library twice.
- Hiding important text behind scripts that may fail.
- Targeting auto-generated names that can change.
- Adding animation to everything on the page.

## Who this service is for

This service suits designers who built a site in Webflow and hit a limit, business owners who need a custom form or calculator, and teams that bought a widget and cannot get it to look right. It also fits sites where earlier code is causing trouble and needs tidying.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of the feature, links to any widget or service involved and the pages where it should appear. We never need your password. We work as a collaborator in your project, and you keep the code and the site.
